judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's readings are all correct and I verified each against the rendered figures and the .tex. The picture graph draws Ana 5 icons, Ben 3, Cara 6, Dev 2 whole plus one half-width icon (worksheet.tex draws the last as a 0.22 cm box against the 0.44 cm full icon), so at 4 books an icon: Ana 20, Ben 12, Cara 24, Dev 10. The pgfplots bar chart plots (Mon,8) (Tue,7) (Wed,12) (Thu,10) (Fri,4) on a 0-14 axis ticked by twos, so Wednesday is 12, Tuesday's bar genuinely stops halfway between the 6 and 8 grid lines, and the week totals 41. Item 8 is correctly typed manual and the judge's manual_items_reviewed: 1 matches. What the judge did not test is verification COVERAGE, and it is the run's dominant defect showing up here at scale: six of the eight problems print more answer blanks than verify.json covers. Problem 1 prints 'Ana's pictures: ____' and 'Books Ana read: ____' against one entry (20) — the icon count 5 is unchecked. Problem 3 prints three blanks ('Cara read ____ books. Ana read ____ books.' then the difference) against one entry (4) — and the judge itself computed 'Cara 24' in its own critical observations, a value verify.json never records as an expected answer. Problem 5 prints six blanks (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, then the total) against one entry (41). Problem 6 prints three (the two bracketing grid lines, then Tuesday's value) against one (7). Problem 7 prints three (a whole picture is worth ____, a half is worth ____, Dev read ____) against one (10). Problem 2 prints two (the skip-count, then the total) against one (12). The answer key does print all of these — as \ans{5}, \ans{24}, \ans{20}, \ans{8}, \ans{7}, \ans{6}, \ans{4}, \ans{2} — but none is bound to a verification entry, and the Quick Answers bank prints exactly one value per problem, so a grader marking from the bank cannot mark the sheet.

strengths_to_preserve: The scaffold design itself is genuinely good and should NOT be removed by the fix: making the child write the icon count before the book count (problem 1), the five bar readings before the total (problem 5), and the two bracketing grid lines before the halfway value (problem 6) is exactly how a scaled-graph reader is built. The remedy is to verify those slots, not to delete them.

Problem 6 is the sharpest item on the sheet: Tuesday's bar deliberately stops halfway between labelled grid lines, and the trap is declared as 'read the top of the bar at the nearest labelled line instead of halfway between two lines' with value 8, so the most likely wrong answer is machine-proved distinguishable from 7.
Problem 7's half-icon is drawn as a genuine half-width box rather than described in words, and its trap (3 whole pictures x 4 = 12) is declared, so the picture and the misconception line up.

The answer key's coaching notes are written for the adult in the room and name the conversation rather than the correction — 'when you hear a number that is much too small, do not correct it: point at the key and ask "what is one picture worth?"', and on problem 3, 'this is the most useful conversation on the whole sheet — worth having even if they got it right.'

Item 8's manual desc is a real rubric, listing the wordings that earn full credit and two that do not ('Jo counted wrong', 'Jo should have looked at the graph better'), which is more useful to a grader than a single model answer.

root_causes.description: Nothing compares the number of answer blanks a problem prints with the number of verify entries covering that id. tests/check_layout.py's answer-location rule only fires when a region has NO answer macro, and it exempts \problem regions entirely because the macro emits its own line; tests/check_answer_line.py reads verify.json but only to bind declared units. So a scaffolded multi-blank item ships with one check and seven unchecked printed answers, and the gate chain reports the sheet fully verified (machine_observation: unique_verified_problems 8 of 8).
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 1 ends '\noindent Ana's pictures:~\ansblank \qquad Books Ana read:~\ansblank' — two blanks; verify.json id 1 has one entry, read_data value Ana = 20.
worksheet.pdf problem 5 prints 'Mon ____ Tue ____ Wed ____ Thu ____ Fri ____' and 'Bikes altogether: ____' — six blanks; verify.json id 5 is a single stats sum entry, expected 41.

worksheet.pdf problem 3 prints 'Cara read ____ books. Ana read ____ books.' and 'Cara read ____ more books than Ana.' — three blanks; verify.json id 3 is a single read_data difference entry, expected 4.

answer_key.tex lines 24, 46-47, 74-75, 88-89, 104-105 print \ans{5}, \ans{24}, \ans{20}, \ans{8}, \ans{7}, \ans{12}, \ans{10}, \ans{4}, \ans{6}, \ans{8}, \ans{4}, \ans{2} — twelve boxed values across problems whose verify entries supply seven.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints one value per problem (1. 20, 2. 12, 3. 4, 4. 12, 5. 41, 6. 7, 7. 10, 8. —).
tests/check_layout.py line 399: the rule reports only 'items {noans} have no designated answer location', never a count mismatch.

improvements.title: Count printed answer blanks per problem and require one covered verify entry for each
improvements.proposed_change: Extend tests/check_answer_line.py, which already receives the worksheet .tex and verify.json and already runs as build.sh gate 10. For each region returned by _tex_segments.segment_spans, count \ansblank, \ansline and \answerline occurrences (plus the single line the \problem macro emits when its workspace argument is positive, so a sheet that relies on the macro is not double-counted), and compare with the number of verify entries for that id carrying an 'expected' value or "type": "manual". Exit 1 on an undercount, printing the problem number, both counts and the two remedies. For curr-096 the content fix is purely additive JSON: id 1 gains a read_data entry for Ana's icon count (5), id 3 gains value entries for Cara (24) and Ana (20), id 5 gains the five per-day values, id 6 gains the bracketing grid lines 6 and 8, id 7 gains the icon value 4 and the half-icon value 2, and id 2 gains a manual (or dropped) entry for the written skip-count. Every one of those numbers is already printed in the answer key, so the sheet does not change — only the record of what was proved.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/slot_undercount_graphs/ with a worksheet whose problem 1 prints two blanks ('Ana's pictures:~\ansblank \qquad Books Ana read:~\ansblank') and a verify.json holding one id-1 read_data entry (expected 20). Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 with a message naming problem 1 and '2 printed answer slots, 1 covered'. Add the icon-count entry (expected 5) and assert the same invocation exits 0. Include a second fixture problem carrying six blanks against one stats entry so the multi-blank case is exercised too.
improvements.expected_impact: The largest single verification gap in the run (61 cases) closes. On this sheet it takes coverage from 7 checked values to 19 and makes the Quick Answers bank a usable marking sheet: today a grader reading '5. 41' has to mark six blanks from one number. It also removes the risk that an unbound \ans value in the key drifts from the figure it describes, since nothing currently checks those twelve boxed numbers against anything.
improvements.risk: Scaffold blanks are deliberate on early-elementary sheets and a gate that demands JSON for each could push authors to strip them, which would make the sheets worse. The failure message must lead with 'declare the value' and offer 'merge the lines' second, and SKILL.md should say explicitly that scaffolds are encouraged provided their answers are recorded. There is also a counting subtlety around the \problem macro's auto-emitted line; get that right in the fixture or the gate will false-fail every \problem-style sheet.

case_summary: The graph reading is correct and the figures are well made: I checked the picture graph icon by icon (5, 3, 6, and 2 whole plus a genuine half-width icon) and the pgfplots bar chart against its coordinates, and every judge-quoted value — 20, 12, 24, 12, 41, 7, 10 — holds, with item 8 properly declared manual and given a real grading rubric. The scaffolding is thoughtful: the child writes the icon count before the book count, the five bar readings before the week total, the two bracketing grid lines before the halfway value. That scaffolding is also where the case fails. Six of eight problems print more answer blanks than verify.json covers — problem 5 alone prints six blanks against a single sum entry — so of roughly nineteen numbers a child is asked to write, seven are machine-verified. The answer key prints the rest as boxed \ans values that no verification entry backs, and the Quick Answers bank shows one value per problem, which makes it unusable for marking the sheet as printed. Nothing here needs redrawing or rewording; the remedy is additive verification data plus a gate that counts printed blanks against covered entries, and every missing value is already sitting in the answer key.
